name: verne-trilingual-graph
description: Real N-WITNESS case (BACKLOG B4, ≥3 witnesses to exercise the variant graph on real text): the opening paragraph of Jules Verne's '20,000 Leagues' (Pt 1, Ch.1) in THREE witnesses — the French original plus two competing English translations (Mercier 1872, Walter unabridged). Base = the French source. This is a deliberate cross-language graph: it models the structure of the planned Verne digital corpus (one French source text + its English translations collated together), and stress-tests the N-witness fold on heavily divergent witnesses. NOTE: because two witnesses are translations of the third, expect the graph to show wide divergence; the value is whether the engine produces a stable, deterministic graph and locates agreement vs. variant positions, not a tidy apparatus. See docs/development/CASE_STUDY.md.
